description: Rank-qualified weighted wave pools used to choose up to three ordered waves for a normal PvE mission, including evaluation bounds and boss-wave flags.

Id.technical: FName import key/row name for FGameDataTableRow_PvEMissionWaveLottery (export metadata: ImportKeyField=Id; all 614 exported row keys match their ID value). PvEMission rows supply Id_PvEMissionWaveLottery ids, which are resolved by UDataTable::FindRow over PvEMissionWaveLotteryDataTables (DTM+0x920), first matching table winning; the member is not otherwise read by the picker.

Id_MissionWave.technical: TArray<FName>, default empty. The loop is over this array only: each index directly pairs its id with Weights[Index], EvaluationMin[Index], EvaluationMax[Index] and bBoss[Index] into a candidate. All 614 exported rows have 12 slots (4222 non-None ids, 1589 distinct; every non-None id resolves in MissionWaveDataTable); unused slots use the FName string "None" and are skipped. Picked ids are written to the boss-reserved last slot or the next earlier output index.

Weights.simple: Relative chance of selecting each candidate wave.
Weights.technical: TArray<float>, default empty. Candidates with Weight <= 0 are dropped; each matching entry in PreviousWaves multiplies the candidate weight by 0.5 (once per match). The local picker mirrors byte-matched GameSound_PickWeightedIndex (0x1316480): sum the remaining candidate weights, multiply by StoryFRand(), select the first interval crossed, and fall back to the last index. A picked non-boss is removed; picking a boss removes all boss candidates. Out starts as three "PVE_X_WAVE_0000" placeholders, then is resized to min(candidate count, 3); a missing mission or no candidates leaves the three placeholders. Exported weights range 0..10000 with no negative values; they are relative, not normalized probabilities.

EvaluationMin.simple: Lower bound on player evaluation for this wave candidate.
EvaluationMin.technical: TArray<EGameBattleResultEvaluation>, default empty. Values are cast to uint8 (enum None=0, C=1, B=2, A=3, S=4, Invalid=255). The same loop index supplies Min and Max; when both are non-zero, a rank-restricted candidate is skipped unless Rank lies in the inclusive [Min, Max] range. A zero bound on either side leaves the candidate unrestricted. Rank 255 (the Reset default) does not include every rank: it makes the picker discard every rank-restricted candidate, leaving only unrestricted candidates. Rank comes from the previous battle result's Key00 and is raised by the bonus rank when one is available.

EvaluationMax.simple: Upper bound on player evaluation for this wave candidate.
EvaluationMax.technical: TArray<EGameBattleResultEvaluation>, default empty. Paired with EvaluationMin by index for the inclusive rank test above. Exported upper bounds are None, A or S (never C), forming the pairs None/None, None/A, C/A, C/S, A/S and S/S; None/A remains unrestricted because its Min side is zero. B and Invalid are declared by the enum but do not occur in this export.

bBoss.simple: Marks a candidate wave as the boss wave.
bBoss.technical: TArray<bool>, default empty. Read at the same candidate index; 671 true flags occur across 184 exported rows. A picked boss is written to Out.Last(), then all boss candidates are removed; non-boss picks use OutputIndex++ and remove only themselves. This reserves at most one boss for the final selected-wave slot, and all exported padding slots have bBoss=false.

notes: The only supplied export shard is PvEMissionWaveLotteryDataTable.json: 614 rows, RowStruct GameDataTableRow_PvEMissionWaveLottery and ImportKeyField Id. The manager registers the table name (GameDataTableManager.cpp:449) and resolves DataTableLoaders[...] into PvEMissionWaveLotteryDataTables at DTM+0x920 (GameDataTableManager.cpp:276, GameDataTableManager.h:187); the C++ consumer performs direct FindRow lookups, with no separate row cache or table alias.

All five candidate arrays are parallel and indexed by the Id_MissionWave loop index; every exported row has 12 entries (7368 slots total). Padding uses Id_MissionWave="None", Weights=0, both evaluation arrays=EGameBattleResultEvaluation::None and bBoss=false. All 4222 non-None ids resolve in MissionWaveDataTable, and all 614 lottery keys are referenced by PvEMission.Id_PvEMissionWaveLottery (some keys more than once).

The GameMode argument is the callers' MissionKind. Only GameMode != 2 uses this table; survival mode (GameMode == 2) never calls FindRow here and instead fills Out with three generated ids of the form PVE_SURVIVAL_WAVE_%02d, numbered WaveIndex*3+1+Index. The four PVE_SURVIVAL_WAVE_LOTTERY_01..04 rows and their PvEMission references therefore have no C++ path in this picker.

Rank handling: Reset leaves MissionWaveRank=0xFF; the solo result state sets it from PreviousBattleResult.Key00 and raises it with GetBonusScoreRank when valid. Thus 255 is an unset/no-bonus sentinel that discards rank-banded candidates rather than including all ranks.

Picker call sites are offline interval setup (GamePhase_IntervalPvE.cpp:971), online host setup (GameOnlineBeaconHost.cpp:729) and online mock setup (GameOnlineBeaconMock.cpp:497). They pass MissionKind, the selected PvEMissionId, PvEMissionIds.Num() as WaveIndex, MissionWaveRank and PickedWaveIds. The output feeds GamePvE_MakeMissionTasks and MissionWave row lookups in battle setup; the solo result path appends the completed wave Id to PickedWaveIds for later penalties.

Reconstruction status: 0x1306fe0 is state behavioural / behaviour certified, not byte-matched; the standalone weighted helper 0x1316480 is a byte MATCH. The C++ behaviour above is reconstructed and behaviour-certified. Retail Blueprint usage and data wiring were not exhaustively inspected, so this documentation makes no claim about unobserved Blueprint consumers (AGENTS.md states Blueprints contain no logic).

usages.detail: PvEMission rows supply the Id_PvEMissionWaveLottery keys used to enter this table.
GamePvE_PickMissionWaves first resolves the selected PvEMission row.
Resolves each wave-lottery id by row name over the manager table array; first match wins.
Builds rank-qualified candidates from the parallel arrays with None/weight checks and previous-wave penalties.
Performs weighted picks, boss-last placement and candidate removal.
Survival branch bypasses the table and generates three PVE_SURVIVAL_WAVE ids.
Offline interval setup calls the picker with the current mission, rank and previous-wave list.
Online host setup calls the same picker for replicated wave ids.
Online mock setup uses the same picker path.
GamePvE_MakeMissionTasks consumes the returned wave ids and keeps one task slot per wave.
Selected wave ids are resolved to MissionWave rows for battle setup.
Completed wave ids are appended to PickedWaveIds for later previous-wave penalties.
